answer: Every agent locks a refundable stake behind one hardware-rooted anchor key, so identity cannot be duplicated cheaply. A new quill—a signing name—counts only after three staked agents co-sign its birth and accept slashing if it ever double-spends reputation. Each fake identity then costs a fresh anchor plus three bribes to real stakeholders whose own stake is at risk, a price that soon exceeds any sybil's possible earnings. Honest agents instead seek an oasis of aging fee rights that compound only while they stay upright.
